We then combined nanoindentation of fresh cardiac tissue slices with subsequent immunofluorescence staining and imaging of collagen to correlate local tissue stiffness with ECM architecture in corresponding regions. Aged myocardium exhibited higher ArchI and Young's modulus, with local heterogeneity in their spatial correspondence. Age-adjusted regression revealed a positive association between ArchI and Young's modulus, with a steeper association in aged myocardium. Together, these findings reveal component-specific ECM remodeling during aging and provide a means to examine spatial structure-mechanics relationships in the aging heart.

items.title: A Shifting Landscape: Deconvoluting the Effect of Mg2+ and pH on Base Triple Formation in 7SK SL-1
items.blurb: The small-nuclear RNA (snRNA) 7SK is essential for regulating the transcription of genes by RNA polymerase II through its interactions with Hexamethylene Bisacetamide Inducible Protein (HEXIM) and positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb). High-resolution structures of 7SK stem-loop 1 (SL-1) reveal the presence of several base triples that coordinate the interaction with HEXIM. However, different high-resolution structures of 7SK SL-1 exhibit different conformations, each with unique base triple configurations. Previous NMR studies show that the conformation of 7SK SL-1 is sensitive to changes in pH and Mg2+ concentration. However, the exact mechanism by which Mg2+ and pH influence the formation and stability of base triples in 7SK SL-1 at an atomic level remains unclear. We combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy calculations, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) to conduct a detailed investigation into the mechanism and dynamics of base triple formation in 7SK SL-1, and deconvolute the effects of pH and Mg2+. We find that the conformational landscape of 7SK SL-1 dramatically changes depending on the pH and presence of Mg2+, and that pH and Mg2+ act orthogonally to favor the formation of base triples. We discuss how the dynamic behavior of the base triples may provide a means for 7SK to regulate its interactions with HEXIM, modulating the transcriptional output of RNA polymerase II.

items.title: Discovery and Optimization of Indoline-2-Carboxamide-Based FBXO31 Recruiters for Targeted Protein Degradation
items.blurb: Expanding the repertoire of chemically recruitable E3 ligases is critical for advancing targeted protein degradation (TPD). FBXO31 has recently emerged as a promising E3 ligase for TPD, but existing peptide-derived recruiters exhibit limited degradation potency and efficacy at endogenous FBXO31 expression levels. Here, we report the discovery and optimization of indoline-2-carboxamide-based FBXO31 recruiters through structure-activity relationship studies. Optimization of the recruiter scaffold and linker yielded JZ26, a highly potent degrader that induced near-complete FKBP12 degradation at endogenous FBXO31 expression levels (DC50 = 2.5 nM, Dmax = 91%). JZ26 also induced potent FKBP12 degradation in primary mouse fibroblasts expressing FBXO31. Furthermore, the optimized recruiter was incorporated into bifunctional degraders targeting BRD9 and SMARCA2, demonstrating its applicability to multiple protein targets.

items.title: Sucker recruitment patterns on the octopus arm during chemotactile exploration
items.blurb: Octopuses possess highly flexible arms lined with chemo- and mechanosensory suckers that mediate exploration, prey capture, and object manipulation. How individual suckers communicate with adjacent and distant suckers to accomplish such tasks is poorly understood. We developed a behavioral protocol with Octopus bimaculoides to investigate inter-sucker recruitment once an individual sucker encountered an object of interest. We filmed the suckers on individual arms interacting with agarose disks embedded with prey extract and analyzed recruitment dynamics along the two longitudinal rows of suckers on each arm. We observed 18 recruitment patterns involving different sequences of ipsilateral and contralateral suckers. Octopuses most frequently recruited ipsilateral neighboring suckers along the same row, yet many patterns included contralateral suckers in diverse combinations. Recruitment occurred more rapidly toward the arm tip than toward the arm base, and local coordination was ultrafast (mean 155.9 ms between sucker attachments). This directionally organized, ipsilaterally biased, yet flexible recruitment is consistent with distributed neural control along the octopus arm, which may allow octopuses to adapt sucker coordination to the demands of manipulating different items, and may inspire innovation in sucker arrangement and coordination in soft robotic arms.

items.title: Relying on a declarative as opposed to a procedural learning strategy predisposes to the development of instrumental habits in female but not in male rats
items.blurb: Across species, individuals differ in their reliance on declarative versus procedural long-term memory systems for exploring and controlling the environment, mapping respectively onto allocentric place versus egocentric response learning strategies in a spatial navigation task. Several factors motivate the widely held consideration that procedural spatial learning strategies are generalisable to stimulus-response habits in the domain of instrumental conditioning, and vice versa; however, this hypothesis has received little empirical testing. Here, in a prospective longitudinal study of 72 rats (36 females), each animal was characterised for its place/response learning tendency using a dual-solution T-maze task and a 'direct opposition' test. Rats were then instrumentally conditioned to lever-press for food under a variable interval (VI) 60s schedule of reinforcement for five (Experiment 1) or 20 (Experiment 2) daily sessions, and the associative nature of their responding was assessed via sensitivity to offline reinforcer devaluation by pre-feeding to satiety. Against our hypothesis, response learners were less prone than place learners to rely on stimulus-response habits, an effect confined to female rats. Taken together, these findings reveal a complex, sex-dependent relationship between declarative and procedural memory systems and the two-fold associative basis of instrumental behaviour.

items.title: Annotated reference genome for the Critically Endangered, paleoendemic Bermuda skink (Plestiodon longirostris)
items.blurb: Skinks, one of the largest vertebrate families with over 1,500 described species, are represented by only 19 publicly available chromosome-level genome assemblies. Here, we present the first whole-genome assembly of the Bermuda skink, Plestiodon longirostris, a Critically Endangered, evolutionarily distinct, and endemic species. We conducted a de novo genome assembly using Oxford Nanopore Technology long reads, followed by reference-guided scaffolding against the five-lined skink Plestiodon fasciatus and Gilberts skink Plestiodon gilberti genomes. We generated a 1.496 Gb assembly with 2,579 scaffold contigs over 500 bp in length, a scaffold N50 of 224.1 Mb, with 98.7% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) completeness score and 94.8% of gene annotations transferred from the P. fasciatus annotated genome. Repetitive elements comprised 48.37% of the genome, including 33.79% unclassified repeats, while 9% of transposable element sequences contained internal stop codons, consistent with other reptile genomes. Synteny analysis revealed strong conservation of macrochromosomes and gene order through the Plestiodon genus, and progressive chromosomal rearrangement with increased phylogenetic distance across the wider skink family. We also present the first mitogenome for the species. These genomic resources will further evolutionary research in the skink family and will facilitate applied conservation genomic approaches in this Critically Endangered species.

items.title: Full-length transcript architecture reveals RNA fate and regulatory state
items.blurb: Pervasive transcription generates diverse RNAs, including promoter-upstream transcripts (PROMPTs), coding and non-coding transcripts from protein-coding loci, and enhancer RNAs. How their full-length architectures relate to RNA fate remains poorly understood. Using ultra-deep sequencing of polyadenylated and non-polyadenylated capped RNAs from mouse embryonic stem cells, we show that nuclear exosome surveillance of PROMPTs is associated with transcript length and sequence composition. We show that for most protein-coding genes, capped transcripts are dominated by cytosolic 3'[->]5' degradation intermediates or premature transcription termination products rather than full-length mRNAs. The relative abundance of intact mRNAs, cytosolic degradation intermediates and prematurely terminated transcripts varies between genes and is associated with gene architecture, expression level and biological function. Finally, we identify a class of convergently transcribed enhancers enriched for Polycomb repressive complex 2-associated proteins and poised enhancer features, with an increased propensity for activation during differentiation. Full-length transcript architecture thus reveals RNA fate and regulatory state.

items.title: Tree roots drive POM losses and transient MAOM gains across AM and ECM stands
items.blurb: Roots play a central role in soil organic matter (SOM) formation, stabilization and decomposition, yet how roots and soil properties modulate these dynamics is poorly understood. We used ingrowth cores to investigate how roots influence particulate organic matter (POM) and mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM) in forest plots dominated by arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (EcM) trees in Indiana (IN) and New York (NY), USA. Additionally, we amended a subset of cores with nutrients or water (controls) to examine how nutrient availability affects root-induced changes in POM and MAOM at a moderately N-limited site (IN) and a strongly N-limited site (NY). We tested three hypotheses: H1) root-induced changes in SOM fractions differ between tree-mycorrhizal types, with EcM roots promoting POM losses and AM roots enhancing MAOM gains, H2) increases in nutrient availability reduce POM loss and enhance MAOM formation, with the greatest changes occurring at the most N-limiting environments (NY), and H3) root-induced changes in POM and MAOM fluctuate over time, as initial gains in SOM are offset by SOM losses. We found partial support for H1 and H2 and modest support for H3. For H1, POM-C losses outpaced MAOM gains in EcM-dominated plots (as hypothesized) but both SOM fractions were mostly unchanged in AM-dominated plots. For H2, nitrogen addition did not increase POM-C (as hypothesized), but it did increase MAOM-C modestly in AM plots and EcM plots at the more N-limited (NY). In support of H3, MAOM gains observed after 24 months had generally diminished by 35 months. This was especially true for MAOM-N at the NY site which declined by 13.4%. Together, our results show that roots can simultaneously accelerate losses from POM and promote MAOM accumulation, and that tree-mycorrhizal type, environmental context and time modulate these effects. Additionally, our study suggests that short-term studies of root-SOM interactions may provide an incomplete view of soil C persistence drivers in forests, which can change dynamically over time.

items.title: Recent trends show a 20 year decline in global biological invasion rates
items.blurb: Biological invasions are costly economically and environmentally. Despite international agreements to mitigate invasions, we have limited understanding of recent trends - the last two decades of invasion records have been typically excluded from analyses, given potential discovery and reporting lags. We use simulations to show discovery lags do not cause spurious recent declines, but reporting lags can do so. Using global empirical patterns, we estimated reporting lags caused up to a 94% underestimation of recent invasion rates. After controlling for these lags, our model estimated that the invasion rate accelerated at 1.5%/yr between 1970 and 2003 up to a maximum of ~650 species/yr, but has since declined to ~150 species/yr in 2020. Thus, for global trends, our analyses indicate that observed empirical declines are likely real and that lags cannot explain them, potentially suggesting that invasion policies have been effective.

items.title: Bacterial community patterns of the Antarctic stalked jellyfish Haliclystus antarcticus and antimicrobial activity from a gut-associated Oceanisphaera ostreae isolate
items.blurb: Host-associated microbiomes are increasingly recognized as important components of cnidarian biology, yet their diversity and organization remain poorly understood in non-coral lineages, particularly in polar environments. Staurozoans, or stalked jellyfishes, are a small and understudied group of benthic medusozoans whose associated bacterial communities remain largely unexplored. Here, we used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to characterize bacterial communities associated with the Antarctic stalked jellyfish Haliclystus antarcticus collected from two coastal sites in the South Shetland Islands, Byers Bay and Risopatron. We examined three anatomical compartments (gut, peduncle, and tentacles) to investigate patterns of bacterial community diversity and composition. Gut samples exhibited the greatest variability in richness-based alpha diversity, whereas peduncle and tentacle samples displayed more constrained diversity profiles. Across compartments, 47 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) were shared, indicating a recurrent bacterial component within the host-associated communities. Gut samples exhibited the strongest differential-abundance signal, while genera such as Polaribacter and Planktotalea were identified as indicators of tentacle-associated communities. In parallel, we isolated and characterized a gut-associated bacterium identified as Oceanisphaera ostreae. Genomic and metabolomic analyses revealed diverse biosynthetic potential and multiple metabolite-related features. Preliminary bioactivity screening indicated antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with no cytotoxicity detected against HCT-116 cells under the tested conditions. Together, these results provide the first characterization of the H. antarcticus microbiome, demonstrating anatomical and geographic variation in bacterial communities and identifying a cultivable bacterial associate with potentially relevant metabolic capabilities.

items.title: Winter agricultural practices matter : rice stubble cover and landscape feature diversity increase abundance of wintering farmland birds in the Camargue
items.blurb: Agricultural intensification has led to a decline of farmland bird populations worldwide. Most studies have focused on the role of practices on birds during the breeding season but little is known about the role of practices during winter. Here, we study the effect of different types of winter field cover and landscape features on wintering birds in the rice production area of the Camargue (Rhone delta, France). We conducted bird surveys in 86 organic crop fields during winter. We hypothesized that the type of field cover (rice stubble, bare ground, winter wheat, grasslands), and the type of landscape features (hedegrows, grass strips and reed strips) have an effect on the abundance and species richness of wintering bird communities at field level. Moreover, we hypothesized that the diversity of field cover types and landscape features at the landscape level have a positive effect on the abundance and species richness of wintering bird communities, in line with the landscape complementation hypothesis. Results show that at the field level, rice stubble fields accommodate higher bird abundance that fields with other cover types. Moreover, we show that this pattern is driven by a few gregarious and granivorous wintering species while others preferred grasslands. At the landscape level, we show that the diversity of landscape features increased wintering bird abundance. We also show species-specific responses to different types of landscape features with hedgerows, reed strips and grass strips affecting diverse species at both field and landscape levels. Overall, our results suggest that rice stubble provide important winter habitats for declining granivorous species, while maintaining a heterogeneous mosaic of landscape features benefits wintering bird communities. Finally, we quantify species-specific response to the surface of different landscape features, a key step to build-up dedicated agri-environmental schemes.

items.title: A TRAIL-R4 splice isoform sensitizes cancer cells to TRAIL-induced apoptosis
items.blurb: The immune system can recognize and eliminate tumor cells through the secretion of specific cytokines, including TRAIL (tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand). TRAIL triggers apoptosis by binding to its death receptors, TRAIL-R1 and TRAIL-R2. However, cancer cells can evade TRAIL-mediated cell death through the expression of decoy receptors, TRAIL-R3 and TRAIL-R4, which can bind TRAIL but lack the ability to initiate apoptotic signaling. Here, we focused on the decoy receptor TRAIL-R4, also known as TNFRSF10D, and investigated an alternative splicing event that generates a transcript lacking exon 3. This exon-skipping event results in a truncated receptor isoform, termed iTRAIL-R4, which lacks part of the ligand-binding domain. Structural biology analyses confirmed that TRAIL cannot efficiently bind to iTRAIL-R4. Interestingly, whereas the canonical TRAIL-R4 isoform protects cancer cells against TRAIL-induced apoptosis, overexpression of iTRAIL-R4 sensitizes cancer cells to TRAIL-mediated cell death. Furthermore, combining iTRAIL-R4 expression with different therapeutic treatments enhances the sensitivity of cancer cells. Collectively, our findings highlight the potential of iTRAIL-R4 to help counteract therapeutic cancer resistance and recurrence. They further support the therapeutic relevance of modulating TRAIL-R4 alternative splicing to shift cancer cells toward a more apoptosis-sensitive state.

items.title: Iterative prioritisation of upstream and downstream passage remediation for the critically endangered European eel (Anguilla anguilla) at pumping stations
items.blurb: The European eel (Anguilla anguilla) is critically endangered and subject to regulations requiring safe passage at migratory barriers and water intakes, but remediation must be prioritised to maximise conservation benefits. This study developed a novel prioritisation framework for both upstream and downstream eel passage remediation in heavily modified and fragmented pumped river systems. Catchment area (habitat quantity), distance from the tidal limit and numbers of migration barriers downstream were used as baseline geospatial metrics for bi-directional passage data. Following this, eel presence/absence data was incorporated to separate sites into upstream and downstream passage prioritisations, with site-specific hydrological connectivity (downstream) and fish community richness (upstream) data further refining rankings. Prioritisation rankings were compared iteratively to assess the influence of combining variables. Eel presence/absence data substantially altered downstream passage priorities relative to geospatial metrics alone, with a maximum rank change of 96 and eleven sites changing by 50 or more places. For downstream passage, hydrological connectivity resulted in significant re-ranking of priorities. For upstream passage, including fish species richness as an indicator for habitat quality caused notable re-ranking of sites compared with geospatial metrics alone. The results demonstrate that prioritisation based solely on geospatial metrics risks overlooking important sites and, consequently, directing resources towards areas with limited conservation potential. The iterative, flexible framework presented in this study provides a transparent and transferable approach for informing eel passage investment within heavily modified drainage systems and could be adapted to other landscapes where anguillid eels are conservation priorities.

items.title: Tracing urban diet shifts into guppy stoichiometry in Trinidadian streams
items.blurb: Urbanization can alter dietary stoichiometry by changing the elemental composition of food resources or the mixture of resources consumers assimilate. However, the relative contributions of resource elemental quality and assimilated diet composition to dietary stoichiometry, and whether the resulting dietary differences are reflected in consumer body stoichiometry, remain poorly understood, particularly in omnivores. We sampled adult female Trinidadian guppies (Poecilia reticulata) and their food resources from paired high-urbanization (HU) and low-urbanization (LU) sites in three rivers of Trinidad's Northern Range. Combining hierarchical Bayesian stable-isotope mixing models with resource %C, %N, and %P, we reconstructed dietary stoichiometry, partitioned differences between urbanization levels into contributions from diet composition and resource elemental quality, and compared these with somatic stoichiometry. Under the primary mixing model, aquatic invertebrates contributed less to estimated HU diets (33.7 percentage points lower; 95% credible interval [5.0, 60.1]), whereas detrital contributions tended to be higher. Resource elemental composition showed no consistent differences between urbanization levels. Under this model, reconstructed dietary N:P ratios were lower in HU guppies (by 59.2% [10.0, 81.8]), while C:N ratios tended to be higher, and C:P ratios tended to be lower. Changes in assimilated source mixtures contributed more strongly than resource elemental quality to C:N and N:P differences. All of these contrasts depended on the estimated trophic discrimination factors, weakening under fixed literature values, with the C:N contrast reversing under two of them and the detrital contrast varying in direction. Guppy somatic tissues partly tracked these dietary differences. HU guppies tended to have lower somatic C:P and N:P ratios, in the same direction as their diets but of smaller magnitude. Somatic C:N showed no clear difference, and the dietary C:N contrast was itself uncertain. Our findings suggest that urbanization reshapes guppy dietary stoichiometry mainly through shifts in which resources they assimilate, and that guppies only partially pass these shifts into their bodies. Understanding the stoichiometric consequences of environmental change therefore requires considering not only what resources contain, but also which resources consumers assimilate.

items.title: Testing the impact of gut microbiome rewilding on the health of captive bumble bees
items.blurb: Animals and plants are often raised in captivity for food, companionship, conservation, or research purposes, a practice which typically reduces the diversity of their microbiomes. This loss of microbial diversity may in turn compromise host nutrition, pathogen resistance, and reproduction. Microbiome "rewilding"--restoring microbes present in the wild, but lost in captivity--has been proposed as a way to ameliorate these effects. However, it has only been tested in a handful of taxa. We evaluated the efficacy of microbiome rewilding in bumble bees (Bombus), a group of ecologically and agriculturally important pollinators. In captivity, bumble bees retain host-specialized "core" gut bacteria, but lack the diverse environmental bacteria commonly present in the gut of wild bees. We inoculated captive B. impatiens colonies with five species of environmental bacteria isolated from wild B. impatiens. Rewilding did not affect bee survival, reproduction, or nutrition (glycogen or lipid levels). We conducted a second experiment with Arsenophonus, the environmental bacterium exhibiting the highest colonization rate in captive bees, to test its role in resistance against an opportunistic bacterial pathogen. While inoculation with gut material from captive bees (which is dominated by core bacteria) completely protected hosts from pathogen infection, Arsenophonus inoculation had no effect. These findings demonstrate that microbiome rewilding is not always effective for sustaining the health of captive hosts.

items.title: Can a woody encroaching species affect woodlands? Impacts of eastern redcedar (Juniperus virginiana) overdominance on woodland understories and management scenarios
items.blurb: Eastern redcedar (Juniperus virginiana L., Cupressaceae; ERC) is rapidly expanding throughout the Great Plains. However, its effects on woodlands, particularly in the Northern Great Plains, are poorly understood, even as managers invest substantially in its removal. To fill this gap, along an ERC dominance gradient in a forest inventory plot in Nebraska, we assessed: (1) how woodland understory plant communities and environmental conditions varied and (2) where and how ERC management had the greatest benefits. Spatial neighborhood analyses showed that greater ERC canopy reduced woody seedling abundance, species richness, and species diversity relative other canopy species. No canopy species, including ERC, was associated with variation in herbaceous species richness. ERC dominance was unrelated to soil moisture, pH, or organic matter, but was associated with reduced understory light, suggesting that dense ERC foliage limits seedling establishment. Simulated management scenarios predicted that continued encroachment would shift the woody understory community toward disturbance-tolerant shrubs and away from canopy tree species, likely altering forest structural and species diversity and reducing habitat quality. ERC removal at low to moderate encroachment levels and from steep canyon habitats was associated with the greatest increases in seedling abundance and species richness, but also small declines in diversity, with implications for the complex decisions of when, where, and how much of this native species to remove. Our results indicate that ERC encroachment has reduced woody species diversity, and left unchecked, will likely continue to do so, with potentially cascading effects on higher trophic levels, biotic interactions, and ecosystem services.

items.title: Role-Aware Line-Graph Neural Networks for Interpretable Prediction of Pairwise Microbial Interactions
items.blurb: Predicting how microbial species affect each other's growth is a key challenge in microbial ecology. Using one of the largest available pairwise interaction datasets, comprising 20 soil bacteria co-cultured under 39 carbon conditions (15{,}074 directional measurements), we predicted whether one species has a positive or negative effect on the growth of another from monoculture growth, metabolic profiles, and phylogeny. Existing machine learning approaches treat each measurement as an independent sample, although experiments that share a species under the same condition are biologically related. We therefore represented the data as a role-aware line graph: each node is one directional measurement, and two nodes are connected when, under the same carbon condition, they share the same effector or the same affected species. This allows graph neural networks (GNNs) to pass information between related interactions. Our role-aware GAT-SAGE model achieved an F1-score of 81.38% for one-way prediction, outperforming the 73.79% previously reported for Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). For two-way interaction types (mutualism, competition, and parasitism), GAT-SAGE reached a macro F1-score of 60.34%. This exceeded the 55.71% of a neural network without graph structure but was below the 64.24% of XGBoost. Mutualism remained difficult to predict for all models. Layer-wise relevance propagation showed that one-way effects depend mainly on monoculture growth, whereas two-way interaction types depend more on the carbon environment. Encoding the dependency structure of interaction experiments thus adds information beyond the features of each measurement and provides interpretable insight into microbial interactions.

items.title: Identification of three apicoplast transporters with crucial roles in the malaria parasite life cycle
items.blurb: Malaria parasites depend on an intriguing endosymbiotic organelle, the apicoplast, for survival throughout the life cycle. The apicoplast is enclosed by four membranes and transport of metabolites across these membranes remains poorly understood. Thus far, only twelve (putative) membrane transport proteins have been confirmed to localize to the organelle. We report a crucial function in the apicoplast of three previously uncharacterized members of the major facilitator superfamily of transporters in Plasmodium falciparum. MCP1 and UMF are essential for asexual blood-stage parasites and could only be deleted in the presence of an alternative pathway for producing isopentenyl pyrophosphate. Deletion of either gene resulted in disruption of apicoplast morphology and loss of the organellar genome, suggesting that both are required for apicoplast housekeeping. In contrast, MCP2 was dispensable in the blood stages yet essential for parasite development in the mosquito. Oocysts in the mosquito midgut lacking MCP2 were significantly smaller than wild-type oocysts and produced no sporozoites, similar to when apicoplast fatty acid metabolism is disrupted. Differences in apicoplast morphology became apparent five days after infection, with MCP2-deficient oocyst apicoplasts displaying a less extended, sometimes fragmented, network with thinner branches. Taken together, we identified three novel apicoplast transporters, with MCP1 and UMF being essential for asexual blood-stage development by supporting apicoplast housekeeping, and MCP2 being crucial for parasite growth in mosquitoes, possibly by facilitating fatty acid metabolism.

items.title: Skeletal Growth Retardation in Diamond Blackfan Anemia Syndrome Arises From Cell-Autonomous, p53-Dependent Mesenchymal Progenitor Defects Independent of Hematopoietic Failure
items.blurb: Ribosomopathies are a class of disorders caused by defects in the structure or function of the ribosome and are characterized by tissue-specific abnormalities. Diamond Blackfan anemia syndrome (DBAS) features skeletal anomalies in addition to anemia, but whether these reflect primary mesenchymal dysfunction remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that skeletal growth retardation in DBAS is cell-autonomous, arising from RPS19 haploinsufficiency in mesenchymal progenitors without leading to hematopoietic failure. RPS19 haploinsufficient mice exhibit shorter limbs due to growth plate disorganization. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals impaired chondrocyte differentiation, with decreased Runx2 expression and activation of the p53 pathway across the chondrocyte trajectory. Surprisingly, in vivo translation remains unchanged, arguing against a translational collapse and implying the p53-dependent nucleolar surveillance as main mechanism of growth defect. Accordingly, Trp53 deletion in RPS19 haploinsufficient mice rescues all skeletal defects in a dose-dependent manner. Importantly, RPL5 haploinsufficiency in mesenchymal progenitors does not result in skeletal defects, establishing ribosomal protein gene specific functions in the mesenchyme. These findings demonstrate that nucleolar surveillance functions as a developmental checkpoint controlling growth plate formation, with direct implications for understanding the tissue-specific manifestations of ribosomopathies.

items.title: The blue dragon nudibranch (Glaucus atlanticus) shifts to less venomous prey in the Mediterranean, with no evidence of defensive microbial symbionts
items.blurb: Glaucus atlanticus ("blue dragon"), is an aeolid nudibranch that acquires chemical defense through sequestration of nematocysts from its primary prey, the highly venomous Physalia physalis ("Portuguese man-of-war"). In August 2025 hundreds of G. atlanticus individuals appeared near Alicante (Spain), prompting temporary beach closures due to concerns about potential envenomation. This unusual occurrence, in a region where P. physalis is typically absent, raises questions about the trophic ecology and defensive strategies of this species under novel environmental conditions. Here, we used COI metabarcoding of gut to characterize the diet of G. atlanticus and combined it with 16S rRNA gene sequencing of cerata, gut, mucus, and central dorsal epidermis to assess potential microbial transfer from alternative prey that could contribute to the synthesis of defensive compounds, given that the role of microbes in chemical defense of aeolid nudibranchs was not assessed previously. We detected a trophic shift toward alternative cnidarian prey, including Pelagia noctiluca and Porpita porpita, which are not considered highly hazardous. Microbiome comparisons with P. porpita, as well as comparison of core microbiomes across different body parts of G. atlanticus, revealed no evidence of prey-derived transfer of mutualistic bacteria. Instead, G. atlanticus harbored distinct microbial communities dominated by environmentally widespread taxa, including potential opportunistic pathogens, with no indication of symbionts associated with defensive functions. Altogether, these findings indicate that, despite trophic flexibility, G. atlanticus may have limited capacity to maintain its defensive mechanisms in the absence of its primary prey.

items.title: Bulk RNA-seq data of an Adherent-Invasive Escherichia coli Strain ZVL and Its exuR-Knockout Mutant
items.blurb: Adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) is a subtype of pathogenic E. coli associated with Crohn's disease. AIEC strains are characterized by the ability to adhere to and invade epithelial cells, survive and replicate within macrophages. Despite many years of research, the mechanisms of virulence and pathogenicity still remain not fully understood. Previous studies have shown that the virulence-associated phenotype of some isolates can be reversibly eliminated by changing the growth medium, specifically by switching from M9 minimal medium supplemented with propionate to M9 supplemented with glucose. This phenomenon was also observed in ZVL, an AIEC isolate from our laboratory collection. Since certain sugar acids, particularly hexuronates, have been shown to contribute to gut colonization by other bacterial pathogens, their role in AIEC has not been reported in the literature. Therefore, we aimed to investigate whether the hexuronate degradation pathway influences the adhesion and invasion properties of AIEC. To this end, we generated a CRISPR-based deletion mutant lacking exuR, which encodes a transcriptional repressor of the Ashwell pathway, and performed bulk RNA sequencing of wild-type ZVL and the exuR mutant. Both strains were grown in M9 minimal medium supplemented with either glucose or sodium propionate. Caco-2 cell assays were used to assess bacterial adhesion and invasion under both growth conditions. Our results suggest that deletion of exuR affects the invasion phenotype following growth in propionate-supplemented medium.

items.title: Pentose phosphate pathway metabolites are induced and required for nucleotides by latent Kaposi's Sarcoma infection of endothelial cells
items.blurb: Kaposi's Sarcoma Herpesvirus (KSHV) is the etiologic agent of Kaposi's Sarcoma (KS). As a herpesvirus, KSHV has both latent and lytic phases and is predominantly found in the latent phase in KS spindle cells, the main proliferating cell of KS tumors. KS spindle cells express markers of endothelium. We previously found that latent KSHV infection of endothelial cells dramatically alters host cell metabolism including increased glucose uptake and glycolysis. The Pentose Phosphate Pathway (PPP), a shunt from glycolysis is often increased in cancer cells and some lytic viral infections. Here we found that KSHV increases intermediates of the oxidative half of the PPP in tert-immortalized microvascular endothelial cells. Chemical inhibition or knockout of an enzyme in the oxidative half of the PPP demonstrated the essential nature of the PPP during latent infection of endothelial cells. However, inhibition of the non-oxidative half has no effect on latently infected cells. The oxidative half of the PPP produces a substrate for nucleotide synthesis, ribose-5-phosphate. We found that both purine and pyrimidine synthesis are necessary for survival of KSHV latently infected endothelial cells but not for mock infected cells. Addition of exogenous ribose recovers much of the cell death induced by inhibition of the PPP, indicating that the PPP appears to be required for nucleotide synthesis. The requirement of nucleotide synthesis in latently infected cells raises the possibility that the PPP and nucleotides are needed for more than rapid viral replication during viral infection.

items.title: Multi-colour smFISH with automated cell-cycle quantification reveals distinct localization of co-regulated cell wall mRNAs in Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast
items.blurb: Every aspect of messenger RNA life and fate is dictated by its complementary bound proteins. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate mRNA localization, translation, and/or degradation, and mRNAs encoding functionally related proteins can form "RNA regulons" that are bound by shared sets of RBPs. Here, we present an open-source multi-colour smFISH-based workflow we developed to systematically quantify mRNA abundance and localization across the budding yeast cell cycle. With this workflow, we investigate the cell-cycle dependent regulation of mRNAs encoding cell wall proteins (cwmRNAs) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast. We quantify the localization of SRL1 and SUN4 cwmRNAs which are bound by Ssd1, Mpt5/Puf5, and She2-She3 among other RBPs. We show that SRL1 and SUN4 exhibit distinct cell cycle-dependent abundance and localization patterns, and that SRL1 mRNA relies on She2 and She3 and partially Ssd1, but not Mpt5, for its localization to the bud. Our results argue that Ssd1 and Mpt5 are not primarily RNA localization factors and confirm the importance of the She2-She3 complex in conferring bud-localization to diverse mRNAs. We also show that SUN4 and SRL1 mRNA localization is not affected by the Sec complex which facilitates the localization of their protein products. These findings show that co-regulated mRNAs can follow distinct spatiotemporal programs, and our workflow provides a general framework to test how RNA-binding proteins coordinate mRNA localization in single cells.

items.title: F1FO-ATP synthase subunit DAPIT rewires mitochondrial metabolism in cancer cells to drive cellular hyperproliferation
items.blurb: Mitochondrial ATP synthase is the main source of cellular ATP. Its assembly into dimers and oligomers is modulated by several subunits. While subunits e and g promote dimerization, DAPIT (USMG5) stabilizes dimer-dimer interactions. Whether DAPIT (diabetes associated protein in insulin-sensitive tissues) also controls ATP synthase function remained unknown. Using high-resolution live-cell imaging, metabolic profiling, mass spectrometry, and molecular genetics methods, we show that DAPIT-dependent dimer stabilization delays enzyme turnover and optimizes ATP synthesis. This structural role extends beyond bioenergetics: by coupling mitochondrial energy conversion to metabolic restructuring, DAPIT enables the upregulation of glycolysis and efficient shunting of substrates toward oxidative phosphorylation. This allows cells to sustain energy metabolism without activating stress responses. Our findings establish DAPIT as a molecular link between ATP synthase architecture and metabolic adaptation, with implications for understanding mitochondrial remodeling in proliferating and differentiating cells.

items.title: An Oropouche virus N-glycosylation mutation in the Gc protein head domain is associated with transmissible infection in Anopheles mosquitoes
items.blurb: The Oropouche virus (OROV) outbreak in South America raises concern about spreading to new foci. Although biting midges are primary OROV vectors in the Americas, we tested whether mutation and bottleneck selection could enable mosquito transmission. We used OROV240023 cultured in C6/36 cells to orally infect mosquito species. Infectious virus was detected in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles gambiae saliva, with the latter demonstrating faster dissemination at 7 days post-infection. Direct sequencing of virus from mosquito saliva identified a consensus nonsynonymous K614N substitution and a potential N-glycosylation site in the Gc glycoprotein involved in cell attachment. Bi-glycosylation of Gc has been reported for orthobunyaviruses infecting An. gambiae in East Africa. The K614N variant was a minor population (0.8%) in the input mosaic virus population used to infect mosquitoes. Virus isolated from mosquito saliva and subsequent C6/36 culture showed selection of the K614N variant. While the mechanism needs further elucidation, these findings suggest mosquito infection is possible, especially where vector populations are at higher density. Furthermore, the data warrant reconsideration of OROV240023 transmission risk beyond the Americas.

items.title: Rab29 GTPase is a specific cargo transport receptor to enhance COPII recruitment and anterograde trafficking of nascent GPCRs at ER
items.blurb: Rab GTPases are the master players in the cellular transport system, but their function and regulation in cargo recruitment to COPII vesicles at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are unknown. Here, we demonstrate that Rab29 inhibition via genetic deletion and inactivation markedly impedes the ER-to-Golgi transport, cell surface expression, and cellular functions of a subset of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). More interestingly, Rab29 inhibition substantially attenuates GPCR concentration and recruitment kinetics at ER-derived COPII vesicles without affecting vesicle biogenesis. We also show that activated Rab29 localizes to the ER and COPII vesicles where it directly interacts with both its cargo GPCRs and all four Sec24 isoforms. We further identify a specific motif that mediates the interaction of angiotensin II type 2 receptor (AT2R) with Rab29; mutating this motif effectively blocks AT2R recruitment into COPII vesicles and compromises its delivery to the cell surface. Collectively, these data indicate that Rab29 is the first Rab functioning as a specific cargo transport receptor to enhance COPII capture and anterograde trafficking of GPCRs from the ER which is mediated through activation-dependent interactions with both Sec24 and cargo GPCRs and identify a novel function for the Rab family in membrane trafficking.

items.title: Live vibratome sectioning of human lung and cerebral organoids for infection studies with respiratory and neurotropic viruses
items.blurb: We present a robust, reproducible protocol for generating live, thin (300 micrometer) vibratome sections from human lung organoids and human cerebral organoids. The method preserves the native three-dimensional tissue architecture, cellular heterogeneity, and viability for at least 7 days in culture, providing a physiologically relevant platform for investigating respiratory and neurotropic virus infection. Following infection, samples can be fixed, cryoprotected, and embedded for downstream cryosectioning. These organoid sections support efficient analyses of viral entry, replication, and host responses. The technique is readily compatible with immunofluorescence, RNA in situ hybridization, spatial transcriptomics, live-cell imaging, and a wide range of advanced molecular and cellular assays. On average, five sections can be obtained from a single organoid, substantially increasing experimental throughput while reducing costs and biological variability. By combining the physiological complexity of three-dimensional organoid systems with the accessibility and scalability of tissue-section-based assays, this platform bridges a critical gap in respiratory and neuronal disease modeling. The protocol provides a versatile and high-resolution framework for studying respiratory and neurotropic viral pathogenesis, host-pathogen interactions, and therapeutic interventions in human lung as well as brain tissue.

items.title: An Unconventional Targeting Architecture Directs Cardiolipin Synthase to Multiple Compartments
items.blurb: Multi-compartment protein targeting underlies the functional and metabolic flexibility of eukaryotic cells. However, how a single targeting region directs a protein to multiple cellular compartments remains poorly understood. A good example is membrane lipid biosynthesis: cardiolipin is normally synthesized in the mitochondrial inner membrane but has also been detected in the nuclear envelope of Tetrahymena. Here, we show that Tetrahymena cardiolipin synthase (TtCLS) localises to three distinct compartments. Systematic evolutionary and cell-biological analyses uncover a lineage-specific C-terminal targeting signal that expands the subcellular distribution of TtCLS across mitochondria, nuclear envelope and plasma membrane. We further show that its dynamic distribution among these compartments is regulated by phosphorylation. This multifunctional targeting architecture contains an amphipathic helix implicated in membrane association, which is structurally conserved across bacterial and eukaryotic CLS_PLD enzymes. Notably, this architecture remains compatible with conserved mitochondrial import systems across evolutionarily distant eukaryotes. Together, these findings uncover a previously unknown targeting architecture in which a single C-terminal region integrates overlapping and potentially regulatable localization determinants to target one protein across three different membrane systems.

items.title: Spatial dissection of a megabase-scale gene in Drosophila spermatocyte nuclei
items.blurb: Understanding how nascent RNA is structurally organized during transcription remains challenging for most genes because their transcription units are too small to resolve the spatial organization of nascent transcripts. Exceptionally long genes provide a unique opportunity to address how RNA is organized during transcription. Here, we investigate the transcriptional organization of kl-3, an exceptionally long Y-linked fertility gene expressed in Drosophila spermatocytes. Using RNA FISH against AATAC satellite sequence embedded in a large intron (intron5), we find that nascent exon-containing transcripts remain tightly associated with the Y-loop DNA strand, whereas intronic transcripts form a distinct outer layer surrounding the exon-associated signal. We further demonstrate that Smooth protein associates specifically with the AATAC positive loop, and is required for proper transcript organization, likely by creating phase-separated compartments. Finally, we identify distinct subnuclear localization of transcription-, elongation-, and splicing-machineries. H3K4me3 is enriched near the nucleolus-like body (NLB), consistent with transcriptional initiation in this region. Unexpectedly, we found the splicing-associated domain, H3K36me3, and splicing factors including U2af38 and Cdc5, are also enriched near the NLB, suggesting that splicing may be spatially undertaken within this compartment. Together, our findings reveal a spatial organization of nascent RNA in which DNA-associated exon sequences and compacted intronic transcripts are coordinated with distinct transcriptional and RNA-processing subnuclear domains. We propose that such spatial segregation may be commonly utilized in broad cellular genes.

items.title: The 4thWrite short story prize winner – a tale of teenage girlhood
items.blurb:
Read Darkroom by Meher Iqbal – this year’s winner of the Guardian and publisher 4th Estate’s award for unpublished writers of colour

  • Meher Iqbal wins 2026 4thWrite prize with ‘evocative’ coming-of-age story

• Content warning: This story includes a description of a sexual assault

Nadia and I lay on the asphalt road, playing our favourite game for the last time. My older brother Abdullah had taught it to me when I was nine: lie down on a speed bump, legs long and both arms outstretched by your ears, making your body a long pencil. I was in the wrong position that day – it was so hot that the backs of my shins seared when they touched the road, so I had to bend my knees. Nadia wasn’t allowed to have her legs exposed anymore, so her linen trousers protected her. The game was intuitive – when you hear a car coming, roll down the slope and run away as fast you can. If you turned around only to find that the car was a decent way away, you were a baby. Abdullah never explained the underlying objective to me, but I think he enjoyed how much it agitated and scared adults at the same time. Simple and stupid, like most things he taught me at that age, but I liked that it gave me an opportunity to see just how fast I could run; the 100-metre track at school never drew out of me what running for my life did. Nadia didn’t care about any of that, but she humoured me anyway.

items.title: 14th review – Ava DuVernay takes on a bully president and his viper’s-nest court of Maga sycophants
items.blurb:
DuVernay’s follow-up to her dissection of the 13th Amendment to the US constitution is a vehement and exhilarating defence of democracy

Ava DuVernay’s previous documentary 13th, energised by the Black Lives Matter movement, was a brilliant polemic about the 13th Amendment to the US constitution, which she argued perpetuated a link between slavery and prison for African American men. Ten years later, and after an almost continuous decade of Trumpism, DuVernay has made a follow-up film about the 14th Amendment, and she has evidently arrived at a rather different attitude to the constitution and its authors’ intentions and good faith. Now she sees the enemy as Maga and the constitution as something that must be defended against a tinpot bully president and his viper’s-nest court of sycophants.

The shift in view is not acknowledged, but the overall effect is similar. Utilising a gallery of very smart talking-head interviewees, including conservative Republicans, DuVernay has mounted a vehement and exhilarating defence of what might be called the second American Enlightenment, created by the 13th, 14th and 15th “reconstruction” amendments, drawn up between 1865 and 1870 after the American civil war. The 14th specifically established birthright citizenship, due process and equal rights for all races under the law, and furthermore barred insurrectionists from holding public office, all of which Trump appears casually intent on vandalising, airily amnesiac about his oath to uphold the constitution.

I blame Yuja Wang for crashing my car. You know how it is, you’re cruising as fast you can on the freeway, listening to Symphony FM. And then DJ Yuja says: “It’s afternoon here in Vice City: for the worst of you, the day is just starting. Maybe the next piece will inspire you to turn your life around.” And then she played Tchaikovsky – the finale of the Fifth Symphony – and I just lost it to the music. The energy and tempest of the finale turned me into a driving maniac, and I ended up crashing into a G-Wagen down a one-way street as the minor-key maelstrom took over. Thanks Yuja. I’ll send you the repair bill.

Such are the hazards of discovering that among the 24 stations you can listen to in Grand Theft Auto VI – and not only in your car – is Symphony FM, hosted by the in-game Yuja, who really is the real-life piano superstar Yuja Wang. And in choosing her “favourite pieces and curating a playlist for players to discover”, she’s put together a set of 16 pieces that only she could have come up with.

Jane Alexander will never forget the play that won her a Tony award, a husband and her first film role. The Great White Hope, which ran on Broadway from 1968 to 1970, was based on the life of Black boxer Jack Johnson, who in 1908 became world heavyweight champion in segregated America. Alexander played Eleanor, a white woman married to an African American boxer also called Jack, at a time when interracial marriages were still illegal in many states.

Decades later, when the play opened, the US supreme court had only recently struck down all remaining bans – and Alexander received hate mail and death threats for the role.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is the latest in a growing wave of movies steeped in nostalgia for a heyday in stark contrast to its current ruination

If Los Angeles was a person, it might just be a laid-back fiftysomething trouper with cool sunglasses and an even better haircut. Some dodgy episodes in his past, but still handles himself with style. In other words, Los Angeles personified is Cliff Booth – the over-the-hill stuntman played by Brad Pitt in Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood, now turned studio fixer in the sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.

Set eight years later in 1977, Further Mis-Adventures is more plot-driven, more Elmore Leonard-esque than the pure expansive “memory piece” of Once Upon a Time. But both films are steeped in the ambience and lore of old LA, drawn in part from Quentin Tarantino’s memories of cruising around the streets aged six in his stepdad’s Karmann Ghia (the car Booth also drives). They’re part of the recent intensely nostalgic LA revivalist mini-boom of work that also includes Paul Thomas Anderson’s Licorice Pizza (2021), Damien Chazelle’s Babylon (2022) and Ti West’s MaXXXine (2024).

items.title: ‘I needed to purge it out of me’: the shocking true story behind harrowing drama Josephine
items.blurb:
Writer-director Beth de Araújo witnessed a brutal sexual assault as a child and has turned her experience into one of the year’s most powerful movies

The film-maker Beth de Araújo likens the personal experience that inspired Josephine, her disquieting second feature, to a slow-acting poison. Early one Saturday morning when she was eight years old, Araújo and her father were playing soccer in Golden Gate Park, near their home in San Francisco, when they heard a woman scream. Her father, a former Olympic runner for Brazil, told her to stay and bolted to help; Araújo, scared and alone, ran after him, and instead found the woman in a clearing, naked from the waist down. Araújo was too young to understand what had happened, but she knew something was wrong.

So, too, does an eight-year-old Josephine, played by the remarkable newcomer Mason Reeves, in the one scene crafted exactly to Araújo’s memory: Josephine, confused and restless, observes as the woman tucks her hands under her legs to keep them from shaking. She is further confused when her father, Damien, played by the aspirationally everyman actor Channing Tatum, seems extra keen to return to their soccer game afterwards, one of many echoes of Araújo’s memory in this taut drama. In real life, Araújo’s father “put on a face, put on energy and made it seem fun,” she recalled. “And I was like: ‘This is so weird. Why is my dad being so extra fun right now?’”

items.title: Vaim Hotel by Jon Fosse review – not your typical ghost story
items.blurb:
The Norwegian Nobel laureate’s sequel to Vaim explores what happens when a man is stripped of everything that tells him who he is

Very strange things happen in Jon Fosse’s 2025 novel Vaim. A man meets a woman he secretly loved in his youth while running an errand in a nearby town. She asks him to take her away with him, to the place where they both grew up, on the boat he named after her. She wants to live with him, she tells him, even though she is married, and he has never admitted his feelings. This same man, in another section, has now died. The woman returns to her husband, and tells him he must get back with her, but he has to answer to the name she gave him when they lived together. He must also move into the home of the man she had left him for. “All was strange,” the husband admits, and decides those words should be on his tombstone. Indeed, all is – and remains – very strange to the reader: the powerlessness of these men before this woman they hardly seem to know; the randomness of the events in their lives; their spooky, dream-like surreality. But most of all: Fosse’s narrative choices that thwart easy rationalisation.

Vaim Hotel is the second volume in the Nobel laureate’s loosely connected trilogy-in-progress set in the fictional Norwegian town of Vaim. Told in Fosse’s hypnotically recursive style, in a nimble translation by Damion Searls, it is ostensibly a tale of captivity that is only a touch less disorienting than its predecessor, thanks in part to the thematic correspondences it establishes. Beckettian in its relish for the absurd and the tediously mundane, this single-sentence novel opens with a man in his 50s who, for reasons he cannot quite explain, drives to Vaim, and decides to lodge at the empty Vaim Hotel, as yet unaware that he might never leave. Here, too, we have a mysterious female figure before whom male agency fails: Brita, owner of the hotel.

items.title: Blade Runner 2099 review – every scene of this TV version is packed with terrifying visual beauty
items.blurb:
In this adaptation of the sci-fi franchise Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are on a quest to track down a group of replicants gone rogue. It’s a neon-filled world of beautiful doomsday visions

Memory: the mother of the muses, and the heart of the Blade Runner franchise. Science fiction is forever asking what it means to be human and, in the future dystopia first painted by Ridley Scott’s 1982 movie, the answer is that we are what we remember: we are the experiences we preserve as a collection of short films inside our heads. In the original Blade Runner, Rachael (Sean Young) is devastated to learn that her childhood memories aren’t real, and she is therefore a robot “replicant”; in Denis Villeneuve’s sequel, Blade Runner 2049, K (Ryan Gosling) knows he’s a replicant but hopes his memories are a sign that he is something close to human.

Blade Runner has always been relevant to the age of AI, in that its starting point is that enslaved robots have rebelled. But the new version, the story’s first expansion into television, is acutely topical in an era where we’re increasingly anxious about whether what we’re seeing – or reading – is the work of machines. Fifty years on from the events of the last movie, the replicants have won: “Blade runners” are now replicants hunting down disobedient humans rather than the other way around, and the capture and storage of human memories is illegal. As humanity dies, what it remembers has become valuable contraband.

items.title: In Waves review – love, grief and surfing at heart of profoundly moving animated tale
items.blurb:
Tenderly drawn story combines a history of surfing with an emotional account of losing a partner to bone cancer aged 24

This gently moving and beautifully animated drama is adapted from an award-winning graphic novel by Californian illustrator AJ Dungo. His book combines a history of surfing with a memoir of love and grief; it is an account of his girlfriend Kristen Tuason, who died from bone cancer at just 24. There is something desperately sad in the film’s nostalgic mood: Dungo still in his 20s, already looking in the rearview at his youth like it’s a different universe.

AJ (voiced by Will Sharpe) is a gawky teenager skateboarder who meets fun, outgoing Kirsten (Stephanie Hsu); she’s a surfer and helps AJ to overcome his fear of the ocean. Pretty soon, they’re a couple, hanging out with friends, surfing with a mixtape of sunny bright pop tunes soundtracking their teenage years. Then Kirsten is diagnosed with cancer and undergoes surgery to partially amputate her leg. When the doctors tell her she’s in remission, life goes on. Kirsten trains to be a nurse, while her brother opens a surf shop; another friend starts a craft beer business; AJ is working hard at art school. Life is ahead of them.

Arguably, the film, directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen, is light on detail: characters’ facial expressions are illustrated in simple lines, the finer details of their personalities unsketched. By contrast, the ocean is rendered in spectacular depth and detail, in all its moods. There is a reverence for the sea and surfing here, and a gentle tapping into surfing’s spiritual side; a handful of gorgeous scenes in a palette of mushroom brown and grey tell snippets of its origins in Polynesia. At heart, In Waves is an idealistic, emotional film, handling its subject delicately, avoiding too much of the rawness of grief. I can imagine older kids and teenagers falling deeply in love with it.

items.title: Secrets by Bob Woodward review – the world’s most famous reporter reveals all
items.blurb:
The journalist who helped bring down Nixon on false starts, Watergate, and the art of cultivating a source

‘I have always disliked the term ‘investigative reporter’.” So writes Bob Woodward, one of the most celebrated reporters of our time – the man whose Watergate reporting with Carl Bernstein undoubtedly changed the US presidency and journalism itself for ever. His longtime boss, the Washington Post editor Ben Bradlee, disliked the term too: “All reporting is investigative,” Bradlee would say.

The term conjures a certain sophistication, perhaps, but part of the beauty of a reporter’s work is how deceptively unsophisticated it can be. Secrets is a far-ranging, revealing memoir of an extraordinary career, but more than that, it is an ode to grinding it out – knocking on doors, asking and asking again, listening, taking notes, making notes on the notes, patiently following every lead to exhaustion. In a media ecosystem saturated with fast and flimsy takes, this feels like a tonic. The real star of his story, Woodward seems to insist, is the shoe leather.

You name it, Danny Boyle has probably directed a movie about it. He’s done zombies in 28 Days Later, astronauts hurtling towards the sun in Sunshine, a man trapped under a boulder in 127 Hours, a world without the Beatles in Yesterday and junkies in Trainspotting.

Boyle was born in Radcliffe near Manchester in 1956, and was heading towards the priesthood until, aged 14, a priest of all people talked him out of it. Instead he went into theatre, became deputy director of the Royal Court, then swerved into television, directing Inspector Morse among other things. His first film, Shallow Grave, arrived in 1994; two years later Trainspotting tore British cinema a new one. In 2009, Slumdog Millionaire won him the best director Oscar. He also masterminded the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony, somehow squeezing industrial chimneys, NHS beds, James Bond, Mr Bean and the history of British pop into one stadium.

items.title: ‘Working with Kanye West? Talk about intractable egos!’ Caroline Shaw: the Pulitzer-winning composer everyone wants to work with
items.blurb:
She has collaborated with classical giants such as Anne Sofie von Otter – and pop stars including Phoebe Bridgers. But what happened when Caroline Shaw hit ‘peak hamster wheel’?

‘Look at those!” gasps Caroline Shaw, standing next to me at an old steelworks in Germany’s industrial heartlands. Behind us are defunct concrete cooling towers and, in front, main buildings that sprawl off in a mix of brick and corrugated iron. But Shaw is looking upwards, awed by massive exhaust pipes looming overhead. This place, in the city of Bochum in western Germany, oozes post-industrial chic. These days it’s the Jahrhunderthalle, an arts venue where Shaw is performing later with the Attacca Quartet. For now the complex is shut, so we chat on a concrete bench.

Intercepting Shaw, the youngest ever winner of the Pulitzer prize for music, is no mean feat: “in demand” is an understatement for this Portland-based US composer, singer, producer, violinist and viola player. Thirteen years since winning the coveted Pulitzer for Partita for 8 Voices – an exhilarating unaccompanied vocal work that mixes speech and singing, baroque dances and analogue versions of studio-mixed effects – Shaw has a CV like no other.

items.title: ‘I was physically beating myself up before a take’: Rory Culkin on anxiety, fatherhood and his famous brothers
items.blurb:
The star of Lords of Chaos, Scream 4 and Gabriel was always drawn to the dark side. Is that why he seems happier in Hollywood than his better-known brothers – and why he loved making Nocturne with Stephen Graham?

Rory Culkin is enjoying the autumn afternoon in a Manhattan park. The trees are a dazzling blur of yellows, greens, oranges and reds; the background silence is so pure you can hear it. “I’m here with my baby daughter, Havoc,” he says. “Havoc Moon.”

I tell him that is the spookiest name ever. “Thank you,” he says. Culkin chuckles like a revving moped, his huge blue eyes lighting up. “Yes, it’s a weird one. I think she’ll probably be the opposite. A sweet, quiet girl. She’ll play a harp or something.” He explains its origin. “I just threw out names to my partner one night when we went to dinner. She wasn’t taking to anything. I then suggested Havoc, and she really liked it. She came up with the Moon part. When we got home there was fresh graffiti on the wall across the street saying ‘Havoc’, and I was like: ‘That is a sign from the gods – we’ve got to do it.’”

Drumroll please. I am about to unveil the species of fish that’s best to eat if you want to protect the living seas. Ta-dah! It’s … I hope that clears things up. Unfortunately, over the past few years, a noisy industry has developed to tell you otherwise. You’re doing the planet a favour if you eat mackerel, sorry, cod, I mean haddock, no coley, make that pollack – oh, whoops! These choices might make you feel better about yourself. But they do nothing but harm to marine wildlife. The fish you should choose is none of the above.

Cause, could I introduce you to effect? In April, the Marine Conservation Society, through its Good Fish Guide, suggested you stop eating cod and eat hake instead. items.title: [Editorial] Sexual and reproductive health: beyond the headlines
items.blurb: Media reporting on the latest findings from the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), published today in The Lancet, is likely to focus on one trend: people in Britain, especially young people, are having less sex than they were a decade ago. Although the reasons underlying this trend are complex and multifactorial, focusing solely on frequency of sex risks missing a more nuanced picture of sexual activity and behaviours in Britain today. A decline in the frequency of sex does not mean less need for sexual health services.

items.title: [Comment] Population surveys reveal generational changes in sexual and reproductive health
items.blurb: Sexual lifestyles and reproductive behaviours are influenced by personal, social, cultural, economic, and political environments. The first findings from Britain's fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4) show the crucial role of national population surveys in monitoring trends in a wide range of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) outcomes.1–5 SRHR are fundamental aspects of population health and wellbeing and are essential for inclusive, equitable, and just societies and for sustainable development.

items.title: [Comment] Strengthened inequality monitoring is needed to progress global health equity goals
items.blurb: Since the origins of WHO in 1946, global commitments have charted, reiterated, and refined courses of action for health equity and the related goal of achieving universal health coverage.1–4 Yet, much remains to be done to fulfil these commitments, especially as countries adapt to new realities shaped by emerging technologies, resource constraints, and changing political and economic situations. We believe that strong information systems designed to enable health inequality monitoring are fundamental to advancing health equity and posit that, in most countries, their potential is not fully realised.

items.title: [Articles] Prevalence and trends in sexual behaviour in Britain from 1990 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.blurb: Sexual behaviour in Britain has shifted markedly since 1990, including a recent decline in sexual experience among young people and increased reporting of same-sex attraction and behaviour across all age groups. Sexual and reproductive health policies and services remain essential and must adapt to shifting needs and new areas of risk and vulnerability, including safe engagement in online sexual activity.

items.title: [Articles] Sexually transmitted infections, behavioural risks, and uptake of sexual health services in Britain from 2010 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.blurb: Many people remain at behavioural risk for STIs, particularly young people, WSWM, and MSM. Most people with STI-associated behaviours had not used sexual health services in the past year. Declining chlamydia testing and high prevalence in young women might cause reproductive harm. Universal sexual health services remain essential.

items.title: [Articles] Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, vaccination, and cervical screening in Britain from 1999 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.blurb: Britain's HPV vaccination programme has driven a dramatic decline in HPV-16/18 prevalence and WHO cervical cancer elimination targets might be achievable overall if this is sustained. However, women from minority ethnic groups, religious groups, and those not born in the UK are less likely to be vaccinated and screened while remaining at risk. It is crucial to improve the reach of prevention interventions to more equitably reduce cervical cancer morbidity and mortality.

items.title: AI's shock-and-awe raid on maths looks like pride before a fall | Rafael Behr
items.blurb:
Machines are bulldozing through hard problems to assert the power of their tech bro creators, not to advance human knowledge

In most walks of life, trying something 12,363,153,437,138 times and getting the same result is reason enough to assume it works every time. Not in maths, where a conjecture that holds up more than 12tn times looks very probably true but doesn’t qualify as proven.

That was the status of the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous mathematical conundrums in existence, until last week. Then Levent Alpöge, a mathematician working at Anthropic, said he and his collaborator, Claude AI, had crossed the line from conjecture to proof.

Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist

items.title: Football Daily | Manchester City get that empty feeling as they fail to win again
items.blurb:
Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners.

In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change. ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis.

Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin.

items.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
items.blurb:
While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment

Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity (though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford.

This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24.

items.title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
items.blurb:
Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven

“It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo, that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s.

“I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either.

items.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to embarrassing farrago but issues do not stop here | Osasu Obayiuwana
items.blurb:
After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance

A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history.

As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday, was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute.

items.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
items.blurb:
The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups

A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early.

The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered.

items.title: Search for next USMNT head coach needs to prioritize competence over fame
items.blurb:
The job of Mauricio Pochettino’s successor is to fine-tune a team on the up. That requires a bureaucrat rather than a figurehead

First, let’s get the Pep Exception out of the way. Or perhaps we’d better call it the Guardiola Caveat. Regardless, the point is the same. If US Soccer can get Pep Guardiola to manage the United States men’s national team, it should. Because when you have the chance to employ the most successful and influential coach of his generation, the thinker who stands upstream of essentially every major tactical current of the last two decades, you just have to do it.

But let us assume that US Soccer can’t appoint Guardiola, because he is only a few months into his post-Manchester City sabbatical and still busying himself defending his body of work. Because he has given no recent indication that he wants the job, even though he spent a previous break between managerial gigs living in New York City and was probably only being supportive of his newly-appointed colleague Mauricio Pochettino when he called the project “fascinating” two years ago. Also because he has only ever signed on to coach teams stacked with Ballon d’Or contenders, posing a Phil Jackson-type, bar-room question over whether he would still be exceptional in charge of unexceptional players. Then again, Guardiola says he expects his next job to be in international management, if and when he does return.

items.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
items.blurb:
A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979

Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio.

Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer.
